previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of migraines, pseudotumor cerebri, hypertension, and diabetes was admitted for a severe left-sided headache accompanied by photophobia, nausea, and vomiting, lasting one week. She presented with markedly elevated blood pressure (197/122 mmHg) and a history of home BP readings up to 202/121. A CT head was normal, and lumbar puncture revealed high opening pressure, consistent with pseudotumor cerebri. She experienced transient left lower quadrant pain during the procedure, but CT abdomen/pelvis showed no acute pathology. Her headache improved with treatment, including IV morphine transitioned to oral oxycodone, IV fluids, and anti-nausea medications. Elevated liver enzymes were attributed to excessive acetaminophen intake from concurrent Percocet and Tylenol use; she was counseled on safe dosing and liver values improved. Blood pressure was managed by adjusting medications, holding several agents due to hypotension, and providing a structured restart plan. She was restarted on topiramate and acetazolamide for headache prevention and discharged home in stable, improved condition with detailed instructions on medication management, warning signs, and follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ YO F with DM2, HTN, LVH, diastolic dysfucntion who comes with 
chest pain and new RBBB. pMIBI notable for increased cavity size 
with preserved LVEF and no perfusion defects. Cardiac enzymes 
notable for trop=0.04 in setting of ARF, trending to 0.01 ___Ks.  This pt has a high pretest proability of CAD, but 
based on her atypical symptoms, negative pMIBI, and negative 
CEs, her chest pain was felt to be most likely non-cardiac.
.  
#. Chest pain - Flat CKS. Trop peak 0.04 in setting of ARF. 
Negative pMIBI. Positive d-dimer, but CTPA negative.  Chest pain 
was not felt to be due to an acute vascular event such as PE, 
Dissection, or ACS. TTE showed no hypokinesis or valuvular 
disorders.  Pain was well control with GI cocktail, and pt was 
discharged with Maalox and encouraged to follow up with PCP to 
investigate possible GI causes of abdominal pain.
.
# ARF: Pre-renal in setting of recent GI issues, improved with 
po hydration.
.
#. Rhythm - NSR with RBBB, no events on telemetry.  
.  
#. Pump - Pt with known moderate diastolic dysfunction. No signs 
of CHF at this time.  TTE showed preserved EF with no valvular 
disease or concerning changes from prior.
.  
#. Hypertension - Unclear what her BPs are at home, and pt 
admitted non-compliance with medications at home. She was placed 
on a lower dose of Atenolol in-house with good heart rate and BP 
control, and was discharged on the lower dose, as she reports 
non-compliance ___ feeling lightheaded and weak after taking 
Atenolol at home. 
.  
#. Pulmonary Hypertension - Most likely secondarely to poorly 
controlled hypertension in the setting of difficult to treat BP 
and non-adherance. Also, there is a strong component of 
untreated OSA given pt refusing BiPAP. Pt was euvolemic in-house 
and will f/u as an outpatient.  
.  
#. Gastro-esophagel reflux disease - Pt with severe gerd, most 
likely exacerbated by her body habitus and diet. Continued home 
regimen.  Also d/c'ed on maalox, as this relieved her chest pain 
in-house.
.  
#. Depression - Pt denies any SI, continued SSRi, close PCP 
follow up as outpatient.
